brief.headline: Nifty Gains 1.12% Led by Banks; Rate Hike Fears and Global Tech Selloff Weigh
brief.summary: Nifty 50 rose 1.12% to 25800.6, driven by a 2.49% surge in Bank Nifty led by IndusInd Bank's 8.5% gain. However, global weakness saw the S&P 500 fall 2.02% and Nikkei 225 tumble 5.06%, while a Reuters poll expects the RBI to raise repo rates by 25 basis points to 5.75% in December. Tech sentiment also remains volatile as Anthropic's record IPO gave way to premarket profit taking.

takeaways.text: IndusInd Bank surged 8.5% to ₹1,001 following a return to quarterly profitability, leading gains across banking stocks.
A Reuters poll expects the RBI to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.75% in December due to elevated inflation.
Gold loan lenders Muthoot Finance and Manappuram Finance fell up to 5% as gold prices dropped to a 1-year low.
Anthropic raised a record $81bn in its IPO, reaching a $2 trillion valuation before facing premarket pressure.
AMD fell up to 11% following a short seller report while California's AG subpoenaed Nvidia over former leadership and China ties.
Adani Energy Solutions expanded its transmission capex to ₹91,500 crore after securing a new project in Bihar.

sections.india: Domestic equities closed higher with Nifty 50 up 1.12% at 25800.6 and Bank Nifty gaining 2.49%. IndusInd Bank rallied 8.5% to ₹1,001 on returning to profitability, while hospital stocks like Apollo Hospitals gained up to 4.5% following Macquarie upgrades. Conversely, Muthoot Finance and Manappuram Finance dropped up to 5% as gold hit a 1-year low. Market participants also face monetary policy headwinds as a Reuters poll predicts the RBI will raise rates by 25 basis points to 5.75% in December.
sections.world: US equities closed sharply lower overnight as the S&P 500 dropped 2.02% to 7175.83 and Nasdaq declined 2.25%. Asian markets extended losses with Nikkei 225 sinking 5.06% and Hang Seng falling 1.89%. Global central banks remain on a hawkish stance, with ECB and Bank of Japan officials signaling further rate hikes amid inflation concerns. Meanwhile, Brent crude dropped 3.28% to 88.96 while gold futures touched a new 52-week low.
sections.tech: Anthropic completed its Wall Street listing raising a record $81bn, with shares initially surging 34% over its IPO price to hit a $2 trillion valuation. However, broader tech momentum reversed as Anthropic fell 6% in premarket trading alongside declines in Nvidia and AMD. AMD dropped up to 11% following a short-seller report, while California's AG subpoenaed Nvidia regarding its former CEO and China links.
